fat.title: Fat loss
fat.intro: Fat loss happens when you eat fewer calories than you burn (a calorie deficit) while keeping your muscle.
points: Eat in a modest deficit. Crash diets cost muscle and are hard to keep up.
Keep protein high. It protects muscle and keeps you full.
Lift weights. Strength training tells your body to keep muscle while fat goes.
Walk daily. 8,000–10,000 steps burn extra calories without stressing recovery.
Track progress with waist size, photos and how clothes fit, not only the scale.
train: 3 days full-body strength (squat, push, pull, hinge)
2 days HIIT or CrossFit-style conditioning (15–20 min)
2 days brisk walk, cycling or easy jog (30–45 min)
1 day full rest or gentle stretching
fat.dIntro: High protein, plenty of fibre and vegetables, and controlled portions. Example vegetarian-friendly day, swap in eggs, chicken or fish if you eat them.
meals: Breakfast
Vegetable omelette or besan chilla with curd, plus 1 fruit
Mid-morning
Handful of nuts or a glass of buttermilk
Lunch
2 rotis or 1 cup rice, 1 bowl dal, paneer or chicken, large salad
Evening
Roasted chana, sprouts or a protein shake
Dinner
Grilled paneer, tofu or fish with sautéed vegetables and soup
Tips
Drink 3 L of water, limit sugary drinks, fried snacks and late-night eating

muscle.title: Muscle gain
muscle.intro: Muscle grows when you train hard, eat slightly more than you burn (a calorie surplus) and recover well.
points: Progressive overload. Add weight, reps or sets over time. This is the main driver of growth.
Eat a small surplus. Large surpluses mostly add fat.
Hit protein daily and spread it over 3–5 meals.
Train each muscle twice a week with 10–20 hard sets per muscle weekly.
Sleep 7–9 hours. Growth happens during recovery, not in the gym.
train: Upper / Lower split 4 days a week, or push / pull / legs 6 days
Main lifts: squat, deadlift, bench press, overhead press, rows, pull-ups
Reps: 6–12 for most sets, close to failure (1–3 reps left)
Cardio: 2 light sessions a week to keep your heart healthy
muscle.dIntro: High calories from quality carbs and protein, eaten 4–5 times a day. Example vegetarian-friendly day, add eggs, chicken or fish if you eat them.
meals: Breakfast
Oats with milk, banana, peanut butter and 3 eggs or paneer bhurji
Mid-morning
Sprouts, curd and a fruit, or a protein shake with milk
Lunch
1½ cups rice or 3 rotis, dal, chicken or paneer, vegetables, curd
Pre-workout
Banana and dates with a handful of almonds
Post-workout
Whey or soy protein shake plus a fruit
Dinner
Rice or rotis, soya chunks, fish or chicken curry, vegetables, glass of milk

Chest.info: Pecs push your arms forward and across your body. Train twice a week with a mix of flat, incline and fly movements.
list: Push-ups|Bodyweight|Beginner|3 x 10–20|Keep your body in one line and lower your chest to the floor.
Incline push-ups|Bodyweight|Beginner|3 x 12–15|Hands on a bench or step. Easier on the shoulders, great for beginners.
Barbell bench press|Barbell|Intermediate|4 x 6–10|Feet flat, shoulder blades pinched back, lower the bar to mid-chest.
Dumbbell bench press|Dumbbell|Beginner|3 x 8–12|A longer range of motion than a barbell and it evens out both sides.
Incline dumbbell press|Dumbbell|Intermediate|3 x 8–12|Set the bench at 30° to hit the upper chest.
Dumbbell fly|Dumbbell|Intermediate|3 x 12–15|Slight bend in the elbows, stretch wide, then hug a tree on the way up.
Cable crossover|Machine|Intermediate|3 x 12–15|Squeeze hard at the centre for one second.
Chest dips|Bodyweight|Advanced|3 x 6–12|Lean forward and go down until you feel a deep chest stretch.

Back.info: Lats, rhomboids and traps give you a wide, strong back and better posture. Pull in two directions: vertical and horizontal.
list: Pull-ups|Bodyweight|Advanced|4 x 5–10|Start from a dead hang and pull your chest to the bar. Use a band if needed.
Lat pulldown|Machine|Beginner|3 x 10–12|Pull the bar to your upper chest and lead with your elbows.
Barbell row|Barbell|Intermediate|4 x 6–10|Hinge at the hips, flat back, pull the bar to your belly button.
One-arm dumbbell row|Dumbbell|Beginner|3 x 10–12 each|Keep your hips square and avoid twisting.
Seated cable row|Machine|Beginner|3 x 10–12|Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end.
Deadlift|Barbell|Advanced|3 x 5|Keep the bar close, chest up, push the floor away. Learn form with light weight first.
Inverted row|Bodyweight|Beginner|3 x 8–15|Use a low bar or sturdy table and keep your body straight.
Face pull|Machine|Beginner|3 x 15|Pull the rope towards your face. Great for rear delts and posture.

Shoulders.info: Three heads (front, side, rear) make round, strong shoulders. Side and rear delts need extra attention.
list: Pike push-ups|Bodyweight|Intermediate|3 x 8–12|Hips high, head moves between your hands.
Overhead press|Barbell|Intermediate|4 x 6–10|Squeeze glutes and abs so your lower back stays flat.
Dumbbell shoulder press|Dumbbell|Beginner|3 x 8–12|Press up and slightly inward without locking out hard.
Lateral raise|Dumbbell|Beginner|3 x 12–20|Lift to shoulder height with a slight elbow bend. Go light.
Front raise|Dumbbell|Beginner|3 x 12–15|Raise to eye level and avoid swinging.
Rear delt fly|Dumbbell|Intermediate|3 x 12–15|Bend over, lead with your elbows and squeeze your upper back.
Arnold press|Dumbbell|Intermediate|3 x 8–12|Rotate your palms as you press to hit all three heads.
Barbell upright row|Barbell|Intermediate|3 x 10–12|Use a wide grip and stop at chest height to protect your shoulders.

Biceps.info: Biceps bend your elbow and rotate your forearm. They already work during back training, so 8–14 sets a week is plenty.
list: Barbell curl|Barbell|Beginner|3 x 8–12|Keep elbows pinned to your sides and don't swing your body.
Dumbbell curl|Dumbbell|Beginner|3 x 10–12|Turn your palm up as you lift. Alternate arms.
Hammer curl|Dumbbell|Beginner|3 x 10–12|Palms face each other. Works the forearm and brachialis too.
Incline dumbbell curl|Dumbbell|Intermediate|3 x 10–12|Lie back on an incline bench for a deep stretch.
Concentration curl|Dumbbell|Intermediate|3 x 10–12|Elbow against inner thigh, squeeze hard at the top.
Preacher curl|Machine|Intermediate|3 x 10–12|Lower slowly (3 seconds) for more muscle growth.
Cable curl|Machine|Beginner|3 x 12–15|Constant tension all the way through the movement.
Chin-ups|Bodyweight|Advanced|3 x 5–10|Palms facing you works both lats and biceps.

Triceps.info: The triceps make up two-thirds of your upper arm. They extend the elbow and assist every pressing movement.
list: Bench dips|Bodyweight|Beginner|3 x 10–15|Keep your back close to the bench and don't go too deep.
Diamond push-ups|Bodyweight|Intermediate|3 x 8–15|Hands form a diamond under your chest.
Close-grip bench press|Barbell|Intermediate|4 x 6–10|Hands shoulder-width apart, elbows tucked in.
Skull crushers|Barbell|Intermediate|3 x 8–12|Lower the bar towards your forehead, elbows pointing up.
Overhead dumbbell extension|Dumbbell|Beginner|3 x 10–12|Great stretch on the long head of the triceps.
Triceps kickback|Dumbbell|Beginner|3 x 12–15|Keep your upper arm still and parallel to the floor.
Rope pushdown|Machine|Beginner|3 x 12–15|Spread the rope apart at the bottom and squeeze.
Parallel-bar dips|Bodyweight|Advanced|3 x 6–12|Stay upright to focus on the triceps.

Forearms.info: Strong forearms improve your grip, which helps every pull and carry. Train them 2 times a week at the end of your session.
list: Wrist curl|Dumbbell|Beginner|3 x 15–20|Forearms on thighs, palms up, curl only your wrists.
Reverse wrist curl|Dumbbell|Beginner|3 x 15–20|Palms down, lift the back of your hand. Use light weight.
Reverse curl|Barbell|Intermediate|3 x 10–12|Overhand grip hits the top of the forearm.
Farmer's carry|Dumbbell|Beginner|3 x 30–40 m|Walk tall with heavy weights. Builds grip and core.
Dead hang|Bodyweight|Beginner|3 x 20–45 s|Hang from a bar as long as you can with relaxed shoulders.
Plate pinch|Barbell|Intermediate|3 x 20–30 s|Pinch two plates together with your fingers and thumb.
Towel pull-ups|Bodyweight|Advanced|3 x 4–8|Hang a towel over the bar and grip both ends.

Abs.info: Your core stabilises your spine. Abs show when body fat is low, so combine core work with a good diet. Train 3 times a week.
list: Plank|Bodyweight|Beginner|3 x 30–60 s|Squeeze glutes and abs, body in a straight line.
Crunches|Bodyweight|Beginner|3 x 15–20|Lift just your shoulder blades. Don't pull on your neck.
Bicycle crunch|Bodyweight|Beginner|3 x 20 total|Slow and controlled, elbow to opposite knee.
Leg raises|Bodyweight|Intermediate|3 x 10–15|Press your lower back into the floor and lower slowly.
Russian twist|Dumbbell|Intermediate|3 x 20 total|Lean back slightly, rotate your torso, not just arms.
Mountain climbers|Bodyweight|Beginner|3 x 30 s|Fast knees, hips low. Also a great cardio move.
Hanging knee raise|Bodyweight|Intermediate|3 x 10–15|Curl your pelvis up instead of swinging your legs.
Cable crunch|Machine|Intermediate|3 x 12–15|Round your spine down and bring elbows towards knees.
Ab wheel rollout|Bodyweight|Advanced|3 x 6–10|Start from your knees and stop before your back sags.

Legs.info: Quads, hamstrings, glutes and calves are your biggest muscles. Training them boosts strength, burns many calories and supports your whole body. Train twice a week.
list: Bodyweight squat|Bodyweight|Beginner|3 x 15–20|Chest up, knees follow toes, sit down between your hips.
Walking lunges|Bodyweight|Beginner|3 x 10–12 each|Take long steps and keep your front knee stable.
Barbell back squat|Barbell|Intermediate|4 x 5–8|Brace your core, squat to parallel or deeper.
Goblet squat|Dumbbell|Beginner|3 x 10–12|Hold one dumbbell at your chest. Easy to learn good form.
Romanian deadlift|Barbell|Intermediate|3 x 8–10|Push hips back, soft knees, feel the hamstring stretch.
Bulgarian split squat|Dumbbell|Intermediate|3 x 8–10 each|Back foot on a bench. Tough on quads and glutes.
Leg press|Machine|Beginner|3 x 10–15|Feet shoulder-width apart, don't lock your knees.
Leg curl|Machine|Beginner|3 x 10–15|Slow lowering protects your hamstrings.
Leg extension|Machine|Beginner|3 x 12–15|Squeeze quads at the top for one second.
Hip thrust|Barbell|Intermediate|3 x 8–12|Chin tucked, drive through your heels, squeeze glutes at the top.
Standing calf raise|Machine|Beginner|4 x 12–20|Pause at the top and get a full stretch at the bottom.
Jump squats|Bodyweight|Intermediate|3 x 10|Land softly. Great for power and calorie burn.
